name: Technical Jargon Density
description: Measures the concentration of highly specialized terminology and domain-specific jargon relative to common vocabulary. When tasked with writing on complex subjects, Large Language Models retrieve and synthesize information from vast technical datasets. This often results in 'jargon cramming'—packing an unnaturally high density of specialized terms into short passages to sound authoritative. Furthermore, AI may indiscriminately mix jargon from slightly different sub-disciplines that a human expert would naturally separate or explain. Human writers naturally pace their use of jargon, embedding it within a higher ratio of explanatory 'glue' words.
mechanism: The algorithm cross-references the text's vocabulary against comprehensive databases of domain-specific terminology (e.g., medical, legal, computing). It calculates the ratio of specialized jargon to standard vocabulary. Furthermore, using TF-IDF (Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency) normalization, it evaluates if the density of these rare, specialized terms exceeds the statistical distribution found in genuine professional human writing. An unnaturally high concentration of disconnected technical terms triggers a strong algorithmic warning.
useCase: Highly effective for auditing scientific abstracts, technical documentation, medical articles, and B2B marketing materials where AI attempts to simulate deep domain expertise.
strengths:
• Excellent at exposing 'hallucinated expertise', where AI strings together impressive-sounding but overly dense technical terms to mask a lack of logical depth.
• Operates independently of sentence structure, relying purely on the statistical weight and rarity of the vocabulary used.
limitations:
• May flag genuine, highly condensed technical texts intended for expert-only audiences (e.g., patent claims, highly specialized medical diagnostics).
• Requires continuous updating of the jargon lexicons to recognize newly coined terminology in fast-moving fields like software engineering.
parameters:
Analysis: Lexical Frequency & TF-IDF Scoring
Metric: Specialized Term to Total Vocabulary Ratio
Output: 0-100 Jargon Over-Saturation (Artificial Expertise) Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 75-82% accuracy on technical domains. Best used in conjunction with semantic coherence metrics to verify if the jargon makes actual logical sense.
